{{nihongo|'''Mishima Shrine (Shimoda)'''|三島神社 (下田市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Mishima Shrine''' (みしまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Kakizaki, {{ill|Shimoda, Shizuoka|Q653402|qid=Q653402}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}.<ref name="jinjacho">[http://www.shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4401086 Mishima Shrine] - Shizuoka Prefectural Association of Shinto Shrines</ref> Taking its name from the place-name, it is also called '''Kakizaki Shrine''' (かきさきじんじゃ).<ref>For example, the bus stop “Kakizaki Shrine-mae,” etc.</ref>

=== Overview ===
The shrine is enshrined on the coastal area of the Kakizaki district, east of Shimoda City, opposite Benten Island.

The date of its founding is unknown.

In the past, on the western side of the same Kakizaki district—on the southern end of Nesugata-yama, on the southern mid-slope of Buzan—there stood the {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} '''Takehokotsukuwakenomikoto Shrine''' (たけほこつくわけのみことじんじゃ), as well as the ancient shrine '''Buzan Gongen (Takemine Shrine)''', which is identified with the deity “Jushii-jō Tatsufutawake no Myōjin” listed in the '{{ill|Izu Province Shinkaichō|Q17193087|qid=Q17193087}}'. However, after the shrine buildings collapsed due to a violent storm in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 17 ({{ill|1884|Q7819|qid=Q7819}}), and were subsequently destroyed by a great fire in {{ill|Taishō era|Q329174|qid=Q329174}} 5 ({{ill|1916|Q2087|qid=Q2087}}), these shrines were merged and enshrined together at Mishima Shrine.<ref name="gen">[https://genbu.net/data/izu/misima7_title.htm Mishima Shrine] - Genmatsuko</ref><ref name="engi">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140127-01.html Takehokotsukuwakenomikoto Shrine] - Research on Engishiki Shrines</ref><ref name="city-buzan">[https://www.city.shimoda.shizuoka.jp/category/050201densetsu/111264.html Legend: “En no Gyōja of Mount Buzan”] - Shimoda City</ref>

The Kakizaki area is known as the place where {{ill|Yoshida Shōin|Q559747|qid=Q559747}} attempted to stow away at the end of the Edo period, and statues of Yoshida Shōin have been erected within the shrine grounds and on the opposite Benten Island.<ref>[https://www.surugawan.net/guide/566.html Statue of Yoshida Shōin (Shimoda)] - Izu & Suruga Tourism Guide</ref>
